target.primary: Cunningham and Pellicer, Open problems on k-orbit polytopes, Problem5, consulted author edition1July2018, p8
target.supporting_source: Cunningham, Chiral polytopes whose smallest regular cover is a polytope, author edition25July2023, §4
target.claim: For every abstract polytope of finite rank, a minimal regular polytopal cover exists; it is unique up to rank-preserving isomorphism if and only if the monodromy group with its distinguished generators is a string C-group.
target.quantifiers: No restriction on the number of flags. Covers may be infinite. Ordinary finite-rank abstract polytopes, including ranks0,1,2.

new_written_steps: Relations of an actual flag action split across disjoint coordinate sets.
The monodromy kernel is normally generated by cyclically reduced words supported on consecutive intervals.
A free extension of a string C-group by an end involution remains a string C-group, by amalgam normal forms.
All nontrivial parabolic coset subcomplexes form a factor system with threshold1.
An explicit equivariant quasi-isometry compares the factored contact graph with the Cayley graph generated by all proper standard parabolics.
Full-support periodic words have uniformly bounded projections of all proper parabolic cosets to their contracting axes.
For every sufficiently large integer m, killing the mth power of a cyclically reduced full-support word preserves the entire union of proper parabolics.
Consecutive powers and normal generation make the join of all admissible kernels equal the monodromy kernel.
retained_geometric_inputs: Graph-product normal forms and centralizer theorem (Chen–Heuer §3).
Contraction of periodic rank-one axes and geodesic estimates (Bestvina–Fujiwara Thm5.4,Lemma3.2,Cor3.4).
Convex bridges, quasi-tree and acylindricity theorems for factor systems (Behrstock–Hagen–Sisto).
Hyperbolic embeddedness with the same generating set (Hull Cor3.17).
Elementary subgroup characterization, finite-change invariance and deep filling injective on the entire generating set (Dahmani–Guirardel–Osin).
retained_elementary_inputs: Coxeter/graph-product standard parabolics and Davis cubical realization.
String C-group/regular-polytope correspondence and recursive end-parabolic criterion.
Normal form for an amalgamated free product.

explicit_unformalized_hypotheses: Normal generation by the chosen relation set.
A supply of two consecutive powers in admissible kernels for each generator.
not_formalized: The Davis cubical geometry and the six retained geometric theorem interfaces.
The geometric application proving the power supply.
The abstract-polytope/marked-group correspondence and the complete general theorem.

not_claimed: That finite polytopes with non-C monodromy have two finite minimal covers.
Infinitely many minimal covers for every polytope with non-C monodromy.
An effective bound on the exponent in the general filling theorem.
A full-paper replacement or a new numerical compression ratio.
An exhaustive priority claim based on a finite literature search.
